clauses.reason: The only operative command of EO 8011 is its operative paragraph, which exempts Arthur H. Chase from compulsory retirement for age; the held text reads "for a period of one year ending November 30, 1939". The recital states the President's judgment that the public interest requires that Arthur H. Chase, who the recital says will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service during the current month, be exempted for a period of one year; it commands nothing else. The command is a one-person permission for a stated period, so it ended by its own terms on November 30, 1939; that date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day) under research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md, and the exclusive reading, under which it ends as that day begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see. Later events recorded for this clause: Executive Order No. 8287 of November 18, 1939 grants a further exemption for a period of one year ending November 30, 1940 and recites this order as the exemption already granted; it neither revokes nor alters the period stated in this order, and it is recorded as a later event, not as an end of this clause. A search of the held order texts for this order's number (jobs/claim-kit cruden search) finds it cited only in Executive Order No. 8287 (APP transcription and Photius printing of each), and the later order's own text grants a further period and leaves this order's stated period unchanged, so the stated date remains the first end under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on "further exempt" orders.

research_rationale:
EO 8011 (November 19, 1938, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt) is a one-person order exempting Arthur H. Chase from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year, issued under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a). This is the stale working-text recheck. The earlier claim quoted an American Presidency Project transcription; the working text is now the machine reading of the Government Printing Office printing held in jobs/mabillon-held-printings (grade machine_read_government_printed_copy, acceptable_as_original false; Executive_Orders_7262-8027.djvu; scanned pages 540-541; closing number tag 8011), and the Photius GPO printing of the same order (HathiTrust hvd.hl272j, jobs/photius-gpo-volumes/output/texts/EO_8011.txt) is also held. Standing note: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved. I read the working text in full and compared it word by word with the Photius printing and with the APP transcription: the number, date, title, signatory, authority citation, name of the person and the stated end date agree, and the only differences are OCR noise in the printings (garbled masthead and imprint lines, split or misread letters) that changes no number, date, signatory, name or period. The APP page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl names this order, its date agrees and its text_sha256 equals the held APP file. No page-render row exists for this order in PAGE_CHECKS.csv; the printing text itself carries the closing tag [No. 8011] and the dateline November 19, 1938. The order is one recital paragraph and one operative paragraph (the text contains one "I hereby"), so the clause inventory is one whole-order clause. The operative words "for a period of one year ending November 30, 1939" fix the end of the exemption on November 30, 1939; that is the first end, recorded inclusive, with the exclusive reading disclosed. The packet's later-events and name searches each report 1 hit, and a search of the held order texts for this order's number finds it cited only in EO 8287; I read the held APP text of the later order and compared it with its Photius printing (only OCR differences), and I record it as a later event.
